subject: Science
stem: A farmer grows a nitrogen-fixing legume crop (like pulses) in a field one season, followed by a cereal crop (like wheat) the next season, alternating crop types to naturally maintain soil fertility rather than growing the same crop repeatedly. This agricultural practice is called:
explanation: Crop rotation alternates different crop types (especially nitrogen-fixing legumes with nutrient-depleting cereals) across seasons to naturally replenish soil fertility and reduce pest/disease build-up — distinct from monoculture (growing the same crop repeatedly, which depletes soil nutrients).
